attacks.claim: The STOP and failure fallbacks send patrons back to `NOTICE_PREV`, and new sign-ups are given `phone` as `NOTICE_PREV`. CallNotify ends 2027-03-31 and the replacement is out of scope (LIBSYS-330). After that date a patron who sends STOP, or whose SMS fails twice, lands on a dead channel and loses hold notices. Only the rollback script handles this (print once CallNotify has ended). This breaks the agreed 'no patron may lose hold notices' constraint.
attacks.evidence: "new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`"; "switches every patron ... back to their own `NOTICE_PREV`"; Out of scope: "what replaces calls for patrons who stay on phone after March 2027 (LIBSYS-330)"

attacks.claim: STOP blocking and delivery-failure fallback both depend on the webhook receiver. If it is down, misconfigured, or rejects a signature, a patron who sent STOP stays on SMS while the provider silently blocks sends, so the patron gets no notices. No provider callback retry, dead-letter handling, reconciliation job, or receiver health alerting is specified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: receiver monitoring/alerting, callback retry or reconciliation; "the provider ... blocks further sends to that number" with the switch-back done only by the webhook

attacks.claim: The rollback section says post-launch enrollees return to exactly their prior channel, but new sign-ups are assigned `phone` as a synthetic `NOTICE_PREV`. That contradicts the claim and can put an email-only or no-channel patron on phone on rollback.
attacks.evidence: "Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before." vs "new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`"

attacks.claim: The plan says switching providers is only a config change. The webhook receiver (provider-specific signature verification and callback formats), the provider-side HELP auto-reply, and the 10DLC brand/campaign registrations are all provider-specific. A switch needs code and re-registration work.
attacks.evidence: "Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change."

attacks.claim: The receiver's DB grants (UPDATE/INSERT only) cannot work as described. Matching patrons by phone number and reading `NOTICE_PREV` requires SELECT on `borrowers` and `borrower_attributes`. The plan will either fail or quietly widen the grants. Signature verification also doesn't mention replay protection or timestamp checks.
attacks.evidence: "dedicated DB user with UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`"

attacks.claim: The budget constraint is enforced only by an alert at $450, with no defined action or cap. Uptake is an assumption, the survey says 64% prefer text, and the newsletter promotion could push volume past the $600 ceiling. A hard cap would itself cause lost notices. The Spanish template is also unlikely to stay GSM-7 single-segment once accented characters are used (e.g. á, ó), which raises per-text cost.
attacks.evidence: "a provider spend alert fires at $450"; "Template (English, plus Spanish ...), GSM-7, one segment"
